Enhancing Workflow: New Herdr Mod Integrates Atuin Threads for Streamlined Coding Sessions

04 Nov 2026, 12:24 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: github.com

Overview of the Atuin Threads Mod for Herdr

A new modification for the Herdr application has been released, designed to bridge the gap between Atuin’s activity logging and the Herdr workspace. This mod introduces a dedicated panel that lists coding-agent sessions captured by Atuin as distinct threads, allowing users to quickly revisit and resume past work directly within their browser.

How the Integration Works

The core functionality of this mod centers on session management. When Atuin captures activity in its 'threads' mode, the Herdr mod parses this data and displays it within a side panel. Key features include:

  • Session Listing: A clear overview of recorded Atuin threads.
  • Quick Resumption: Clicking on any thread automatically opens that specific session in a new browser tab.
  • Centralized Access: Eliminates the need to manually navigate through logs to find previous coding sessions.

Implementation and Requirements

To implement this mod, users must ensure they meet the specific technical prerequisites:

  • Atuin Version: Requires Atuin version 18.24.3 or higher.
  • Configuration: Users must explicitly enable the thread feature by running `atuin config enable threads` in their terminal.
  • Installation: The mod files should be placed into the `~/.config/herdr-app/mods/` directory. Following this, the provided `keys.json` data must be merged into the user’s existing configuration file.
  • Activation: Once installed, users can toggle the panel using the keyboard shortcut `Cmd+Shift+T`.

Verification and Safety

As this is a third-party modification, users are encouraged to review the source code on the official GitHub repository before installation. The repository includes a `RECIPE.md` file, which serves as a technical brief for those interested in building the module from scratch or verifying its underlying architecture. By manually reviewing the code, developers can ensure compatibility with their specific environment and maintain control over their local configurations.
